title: LED Inspection - Crystal Originated Particles (COP) Detection on WaferSight PWG
subtitle: Post-Anneal Quality Validation for 14nm Node Manufacturing
author: Lisa Johansson

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the WaferSight PWG system to detect and classify Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects during post-anneal inspection at the 14nm technology node. The test is conducted at Milpitas Fab B to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 450mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects that are critical to yield at the 14nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the WaferSight PWG platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: WaferSight PWG
- Inspection Type: LED Inspection
- Target Defect: Crystal Originated Particles (COP)
- Process Step: Post-Anneal
- Wafer Size: 450mm
- Technology Node: 14nm
- Fab Location: Milpitas Fab B

This test case applies to all WaferSight PWG systems deployed at Milpitas Fab B for post-anneal monitoring in the 14nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: WaferSight PWG
Software Version: v11.9.661
Recipe: LED_INSPECTION_14nm_POST_ANNEAL
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (90 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 3mm
Sampling Plan: 21-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the WaferSight PWG system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'LED Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Crystal Originated Particles (COP) defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 14nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 109 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 90% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.4% for LED Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-04-29
Wafers Tested: 7
Total Defects Found: 3342
Defect Density: 1063.79 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 2.6%
Capture Rate: 95.3%
Test Duration: 162 minutes
System Uptime: 96.0%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The WaferSight PWG demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Crystal Originated Particles (COP) at the 14nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Crystal Originated Particles (COP) at 14nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
